hero.tagline: Where the ember meets the dawn — the old world exhales, and the new world has not yet learned to breathe

today.heading: The threshold hour
today.intro: Where yesterday releases its grip and tomorrow has not yet arrived. A moment of pure presence between what was and what will be.

visualAsset.description: Deep ocean bioluminescence with glowing jellyfish and lilies
visualAsset.credit: Generated for Atrijā daily mutation #852 — bioluminescent garden

gita.label: III. The Paused Blade
gita.heading: Equanimity
gita.intro: The Gita teaches that samatva — equal composure in pleasure and pain — is the highest form of yoga. Not indifference, but the deepest engagement with life as it is.
facts: Samatva is not detachment — it is full participation without being controlled by outcomes.
Action driven by outcome creates bondage. Action performed as duty liberates.

moon.label: I. The Remembering Tide
moon.heading: Waning Crescent
moon.intro: The moon wanes toward darkness — a reminder that endings are necessary before new beginnings. In the void, potential gathers.
facts: Waning crescent is the release phase — let go of what no longer serves.
The new moon follows: a blank canvas, a fresh cycle.

shiva.label: IV. The Sleeping Dance
shiva.heading: Destruction as Creation
shiva.intro: Shiva dissolves so that new forms can emerge. Every ending carries the seed of beginning. The dance of destruction is the dance of renewal.
facts: Shiva's tandava is the cosmic cycle of creation and dissolution.
Destruction is not the opposite of creation — it is its prerequisite.

art.label: V. The Dreaming Brush
art.heading: Seeing Beyond Form
art.intro: Art is not decoration — it is the practice of seeing what others overlook. A single brushstroke can hold more truth than a thousand words.
facts: The impressionists painted light itself, not objects.
Beauty lives in the space between representation and abstraction.

philosophy.label: II. The Unraveling
philosophy.heading: The Examined Life
philosophy.intro: Socrates was right: the unexamined life is not worth living. But examination without action is paralysis. The goal is not to think about life — it is to live what you discover.
facts: Philosophy begins in wonder and ends in clarity.
The unlived thought is only half the truth.
